## My Reasoning

I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over 35 years. I know this county well — flat ground, deep loam soils, but the water table has been dropping year after year. That weighs on me.

The decision is not complicated. I will stick with the **winter wheat–summer maize rotation** that has fed my family and made me a living. It suits the climate, the soil, and the machinery I already own. After the wheat comes off in June, I immediately seed maize into the stubble — no wasted days.

I contract 10 mu of land. It's not a huge operation, but at 60 I manage it well with my son helping during peak periods.

**On seed:** I will not use traditional seed. I buy certified improved wheat varieties — this year 石麦22 — from the county seed station. For maize I always use hybrid,郑单958 has been reliable for me for years.

**On fertilizer:** I had my soil tested two years ago. My fields are moderately high in organic matter. I will apply a bit less nitrogen than my neighbors — I've found 14 kg/mu for wheat and 15 kg/mu for maize gives me nearly the same yield with less input cost and runoff into the drainage ditches.

**On water:** This is my biggest concern. The government has been pushing water-saving irrigation for a reason. I will irrigate wheat three times — overwintering water in November, jointing in April, heading in May. I skip the grain-filling irrigation I used to do. For maize, summer rains usually carry me through; I will irrigate once at silking only if we get a dry July.

**On tillage:** After maize harvest, I rotary-till the wheat ground to chop and incorporate the straw — it helps the soil and reduces disease. For summer maize, I plant directly into the wheat stubble. No-till saves me time, fuel, and keeps soil moisture in.

**On pesticides:** Wheat gets three treatments: a pre-emergent herbicide in November, a broadleaf herbicide in March, and a fungicide spray at heading for powdery mildew and scab. Maize gets two: a post-emergent herbicide shortly after emergence and one insecticide for corn borer around the 8-leaf stage if the traps show pressure.
